title: Introducing Parallax: America's AI Energy Company | Greylock
gist: Greylock co-led the Series A in Parallax, which is building 3D-printed 10MW gas turbines purpose built for data centers. The thesis: the US grid and incumbent gas turbines (sold out until 2030+) can't meet a ~100 GW / $100bn+ AI power shortage over the next 5 years, so natural gas off-grid power with a new turbine design is the scaled answer.

insights.claim: America faces a roughly 100 GW energy shortage, worth over $100bn, over the next 5 years, driven by AI data center demand.
insights.speaker: Seth Rosenberg
insights.so_what: Sizes the near-term AI power gap investors are underwriting: ~100 GW / $100bn+ by ~2031.
insights.quote: Now he’s focused on solving the 100 GW, worth over $100bn, energy shortage facing America in the next 5 years.

insights.claim: The US electric grid is effectively sold out, forcing large new loads like AI data centers to seek off-grid power.
insights.speaker: Seth Rosenberg
insights.so_what: Behind-the-meter generation becomes the default path for new AI capacity.

insights.claim: Natural gas is the only scaled off-grid energy solution for data centers within the next 5 years, per Parallax founder Carl's thesis as relayed by Greylock.
insights.speaker: Seth Rosenberg
insights.so_what: Supports gas demand and gas-fired distributed generation over the 2026-2031 window rather than renewables/nuclear for near-term AI load.
insights.quote: The scaled solution for off-grid energy in the next 5 years is natural gas.

insights.claim: Gas turbines, the most efficient way to convert natural gas to power, are sold out until 2030 or later.
insights.speaker: Seth Rosenberg
insights.so_what: Turbine OEM backlogs extend past 2030, giving pricing power to incumbents and an opening for new entrants.
insights.quote: But gas turbines, the most efficient way to convert natural gas to power, are also sold out until 2030+.

insights.claim: Incumbent gas turbines are engineered for jet engine and large utility customers that demand extreme reliability and efficiency, which requires complex supply chains booked out for years and explains the shortage.
insights.speaker: Seth Rosenberg
insights.so_what: The bottleneck is a product-spec mismatch, not just capacity, so a differently-specced turbine can bypass it.
insights.quote: Meeting those requirements takes feats of engineering and highly complex supply chains, all booked out for years.
insights.locator: Carl made the simple, yet profound

insights.claim: Data centers need power available now, easy to install and easy to produce at scale, rather than the aviation-grade reliability and efficiency incumbent turbines are built for.
insights.speaker: Seth Rosenberg
insights.so_what: Speed-to-power trumps efficiency for AI buyers, creating a new customer segment that tolerates lower-spec equipment.
insights.quote: Power, available now. Easy to install, and easy to produce at scale.
insights.locator: But what do data centers need?

insights.claim: Parallax designs gas turbines purpose built for data centers and uses additive manufacturing (3D printing) to control its own supply chain and produce power at scale.
insights.speaker: Seth Rosenberg
insights.so_what: Vertical integration via additive manufacturing is the wedge to escape incumbent supply-chain queues.
insights.quote: Parallax is able to use additive manufacturing (i.e. 3D printing) to control its own supply chain, and produce purpose built, scaled power.
insights.locator: But what do data centers need?

insights.claim: Parallax's first product is a 10MW gas turbine purpose built for data centers.
insights.speaker: Seth Rosenberg
insights.so_what: Small modular unit size suits distributed, stackable data center deployments.
insights.quote: Parallax’s first product is a 10MW gas turbine, purpose built for data centers.
insights.locator: But what do data centers need?

insights.claim: Greylock co-led the Series A in Parallax, alongside co-investors Founders Fund, Eclipse, Lux, Diffusion and General Catalyst.
insights.speaker: Seth Rosenberg
insights.so_what: Top-tier syndicate signals strong VC appetite for AI energy hardware plays.

insights.claim: Greylock frames the Parallax investment primarily as a bet on founder Carl, a Stanford mechanical engineer who has built over 2,000 components.
insights.speaker: Seth Rosenberg
insights.so_what: Early-stage hardware energy bets are being underwritten on founder execution more than proven product.
